- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >65.00) — apply a “lag correction”: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 2–3 periods post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed — cap forecast at 10% below recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0) within 5 days, model fails to adjust — force a 1–2% downward correction in next 3–5 periods.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid sharp upward moves after 2–3 consecutive low sentiment days — cap slope at 0.5% per day max.
